features.optics-qsfp-dd: 400GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/ER4/LR4/SR8/FR4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4; 200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4; 100GE QSFP28 ZR4/ER4/LR4/SR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list)
features.timing-cable: SMB coaxial with a 10-32UNF-2A connector, for 1PPS and 10MHz
features.zr-capacity: up to 32 QSFP-DD ZR+ modules; the HIG's Figure 12 shades one 32-port band to mark which ports they are - see the zr-port-set gap

management.console: RJ45 RS-232 plus a micro-USB serial console

thermal.airflow: front-to-back or back-to-front, selected by the fan and PSU build

configs.description: Dual 2400W AC supplies (PSU-242-AECRN, C20 inlet, red latch) with front-to-back fans (FAN-805616-HCE). The back-to-front build swaps both for their blue-latched intake counterparts - PSU-242-AICB-NN and FAN-805616-CCD - which are orderable and are modelled only as the fan's blue skin, because no held figure shows the intake PSU's face.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: The chassis as it ships and as every rear figure draws it - four FAN-805616-HCE fans and two PSU-242-AECRN 2400W AC supplies, red handles and latches throughout, front-to-back airflow, and the sixty-six traffic and management ports empty. No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document; see the chassis-sku gap.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Dual 2400W -48V DC supplies (PSU-242-DEERN, two-row V+/V- input block, red latch) with front-to-back fans (FAN-805616-HCE). The HIG rates the DC feed at -48V to -60V for operation up to 5000 m and notes a 120 A fast-acting fuse built into each supply.
configs.name: dc

gaps.note: The HIG's section 10 tables the six front-panel lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the RJ45 management jack, and says nothing about the port lamps. Each QSFP-DD column carries a four-part cluster - a two-window light pipe at each end of the cage width with a round lamp inboard of each - and nothing states which half serves the upper port and which the lower, nor what the pipe's two windows mean against the round lamp. Every lamp keeps the component's off/on default; each cluster's `for` lists the two ports of the column it stands over, which is adjacency and not an asserted mapping. The SFP+ pair has no lamps drawn beside it at all.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: The HIG Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81 x 176.53 x 81.5 mm (W x D x H). HIG Figure 9's rear elevation, which passes the aspect gate at 0.45%, draws four identical faces abutting from x 17 to x 837 px with no chassis web between them, and four independent repeated features on that face - the airflow tag, the status lamp, the handle and the release tab - all sit on a 205.33 px pitch, which is 83.84 mm. The face is 83.7 x 80.0 and the table's number is 81 x 81.5. The likely resolution is the S9300-32D's: 81 measures the fan BODY behind the flange and the face is wider. That is an inference and not something either document says, so the manifest carries the measured face and this entry carries the disagreement.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-805616, or a caliper on the FRU

gaps.note: The ports ARE numbered 0-63 and 64-65 - HIG Figure 10 prints every numeral - but it prints them on the schematic module faces, where a seated module would cover them, so the figure does not say where the metal carries them. Nothing was found on the metal: the dark chassis web between the two cage bands profiles flat with no bright marks, and the 520 px front photograph is 1.19 px/mm, far too coarse for a 2 mm digit. No numerals are therefore drawn, rather than 66 of them being placed by guesswork.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on front photograph at 4 px/mm or better, or a vendor faceplate artwork sheet

gaps.note: Every small legend on the left-hand block is 4-6 px tall in the only orthographic front figure held, and does not resolve at 20x with autocontrast. Their positions and extents are measured; their WORDING is the HIG Figure 4 callout list and the Front Panel LED table's row names, which is a strong inference and still an inference. Four glyphs ARE legible and are drawn as seen: an up and a down triangle above the SFP+ block and another pair beside the RJ45 stack, plus the three-box network symbol to the right of the second pair. Three legends that certainly exist are NOT drawn, because nothing identifies them: a roughly 6 mm word between the USB symbol and the lower up-triangle at x 18.7-24.7 y 77-80, and two small marks flanking the SFP+ triangles at x 20.3-22.7 and x 32.9-35.4, y 12.7-15.3.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on front photograph at 4 px/mm or better

gaps.note: The HIG states the 110 V AC per-supply output twice and differently. Section 7 says 'If power input for AC power supply is only 110V, there will only be 1000 watts per power supply and will not be enough power for the power supply to be changed while the switch is in operation.' Section 9's AC note says 'If only a 110V AC power source is available, the S9311-64D can still be powered with both PSUs providing 1200 watts each for a total output of 2400 watts.' Same measure, same scope, two values. Neither is the number this manifest carries - power-output-w on the PSU contracts is the 2400 W nameplate from the datasheet's ordering lines, at the 200-240 V input the datasheet specifies - but a reader budgeting a 110 V feed needs to know the guide contradicts itself.
gaps.wanted: the PSU-242 supply datasheet, or a UfiSpace erratum for HIG R1.2

gaps.note: No held figure shows a DC build seated in the chassis. HIG Figure 9 and the datasheet rear render both show the AC unit with its C20 inlet, so the DC contract's fan frame, pull bar, latch and lamp positions are carried over from the AC unit rather than measured on a DC face. What is specific to the DC unit - a two-row input block, V+ over V-, with two lug/screw holes above it - comes from HIG Figure 6's CAD front view, whose own scale is only good to a couple of percent, so the block is drawn on the AC inlet's measured footprint instead of on that sheet's scale. The datasheet also names the connector for the INTAKE variant only ('CRPS TE 2204535-3 ELON Mini') and names none for the exhaust variant modelled here.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or elevation of a DC-configured S9311-64D, or the Delta drawing for PSU-242-DEERN at a stated scale

gaps.note: The HIG says 'The 400G QSFP-DD ports highlighted support both ZR+ transceivers up to 32 units' above Figure 12, and Figure 12 renders the lower band of 32 ports (32-63) pale against the upper band's normal dark. 32 is exactly one band, so the count and the shading agree - but the guide never says whether the pale band is the highlighted set or the excluded one, and the sentence's 'highlighted' is not defined anywhere in the document. No port is therefore given a per-port ZR attribute; the capability is recorded on the device as 'up to 32' without naming which 32.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace optics compatibility matrix, or a Figure 12 revision with a legend

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says 'there are two locations on the case in which the grounding lug may be fixed' and then shows one, on the rear panel's right-hand strip under the yellow label (Figures 22 and 23). The prose calls that location 'the side of the switch', which the strip arguably is, so it is not even certain the two sentences describe two different places. Only the located one is drawn; nothing is placed on a side face by inference.
gaps.wanted: a figure or photograph showing the second grounding location

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9311-64D, and the Available to Order block names only the four PSUs and two fans. The S9510-28DC precedent applies: that model's -BN0B/-BR1B SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no held PDF, so orderable SKUs for the AC/DC and airflow builds almost certainly exist. The configurations therefore carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

a top-level `profile:` naming the device class, so that `specified` has something to judge the attrs against - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml for the classes that exist, which unlocks `specified` and with it the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (rear 6); `physical-context` on port groups qsfpdd-400g, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

provenance.attrs: datasheet - Specifications, Performance, Environmental, Regulatory Compliance and Supported Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied. The datasheet's own typo in the weight row ('Weight withou FRU') is not reproduced; the number is.
provenance.chassis: datasheet - 'Chassis (WxDxH) 2RU, 436 x 580 x 87.7 mm', 'Weight withou FRU: 18.52kg'; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple and the same weight. 436 is the body between the ear planes, not a rack face: both front figures draw two small bracket tabs standing OUTSIDE the full-height body on each side (fig-0019 px 4-11 and 1346-1353 against a body of 12-1345), and those tabs are the mounting hardware, which is not drawn here. 87.7 mm is 1.98 rack units, which is why the datasheet calls it 2RU.
provenance.connector-orientation: photo/drawing, checked in zoomed crops rather than assumed. The stacked RJ45 pair MIRRORS: at 16x the upper jack's latch keyway is a notch at the TOP of its aperture and the lower jack's is at the BOTTOM, with the lower jack's two integrated lamps in its bottom corners. std/rj45-ganged draws its keyway at the bottom, so the CONSOLE jack is rotate: 180 and the OOB jack is unrotated. The stacked SFP+ pair mirrors the same way - the cage tab of each hangs into the silver band between them, upper tab down and lower tab up - and std/sfp-ganged draws its cage lip near the top, so port-64 is rotate: 180 and port-65 is unrotated. std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11) is used rather than std/rj45 (16 mm bezel) because the stack pitch measures 14.19 mm, which a 16 mm bezel cannot sit on. The USB 3.0 socket is PORTRAIT - its drawn aperture is 6.2 wide by 13.5 tall - so std/usb-a is rotated 90; the C20 inlet on the PSU is portrait too, rotated 270 so its earth pin lies on the LEFT, which is the side the figure puts the single contact slot on against the pair.
provenance.front-layout: drawing - HIG Figure 12 at 3.083 px/mm across, 3.102 down, cross-checked against the front photograph and the datasheet render. Left to right: a timing/management block at the left edge (two SMB jacks over a reset pinhole, a printed legend block over a column of six lamps, a micro-USB over a portrait USB 3.0), then the stacked SFP+ pair over the stacked RJ45 pair, then the sixteen QSFP-DD columns. Positions read off the figure are good to about 0.3 mm at that scale and are carried as drawing confidence. One feature on this face has no name in any held document and is drawn anyway, because two independent images show it in the same place: a long narrow recess at x 432.3-434.9, y 33.9-64.2, in the blank right margin past the last cage column. It is in HIG Figure 12 and in the front photograph at matching proportions. It is drawn as a dark decor slot and not as a component because nothing identifies it - it reads as a finger pull for sliding the chassis on its rails, and that reading is a guess, so it is not written into a part name.
provenance.grounding: HIG section 8 - the switch is grounded through a two-hole #4 AWG lug and two M4 screws, and the guide says there are 'two locations on the case in which the grounding lug may be fixed'. Figures 22 and 23 show ONE of them: the rear panel's right-hand strip, its two holes under the yellow protective label that Figure 22 tells you to remove. The holes are therefore modelled as being under the drawn label and are not drawn separately. The SECOND location is not shown in any held figure - the prose says 'located on the side of the switch', which the rear-right strip also arguably is - so it is recorded as a gap rather than placed on a side face by inference.
provenance.legend-wording: positions measured, WORDING NOT READ OFF THE ARTWORK. The small legends around the left-hand block are 4-6 px tall at the figure's 3.1 px/mm and do not resolve at any zoom - autocontrasted 20x crops give letter blobs, not letters. What is measured is that a legend EXISTS at each position and how big it is. The words written here are the HIG Figure 4 callout for the feature each legend sits against (1PPS, 10MHz, Reset, Micro USB, Console Ports, USB 3.0, RJ45 OOB) and the HIG Front Panel LED table's own row names for the six lamps (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID). Two glyphs ARE readable and are drawn as seen: a solid up triangle and a solid down triangle beside the RJ45 stack, and the three-box network symbol to their right. See the front-legend-glyphs gap.
provenance.lifecycle: searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9311-64D end of life' - no announcement found; the vendor's data-center product page and the R1.2 hardware guide are both live. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.
provenance.port-numbers: NOT DRAWN, deliberately. HIG Figure 10 numbers every port 0-63 in blue and the SFP+ pair 64-65 in orange, but it prints each numeral ON the schematic module face, where a seated module would cover it. Unlike the S9300-32D - whose datasheet render shows small printed marks in the inter-row web, which is why that model draws them - this chassis has no web inside a band (the EMI strip is there instead), and neither fig-0020 nor the 520 px front photograph shows a printed numeral anywhere on the metal: the dark inter-band web at rows 131-138 profiles flat at luminance 54-57 with no bright marks in it. Where the vendor prints the numbers is therefore recorded as a gap rather than guessed at. The NUMBERING itself is Figure 10's and is certain: even numbers on each band's upper row and odd on its lower, left to right, 0-31 in the upper band and 32-63 in the lower.
provenance.power: datasheet 'Typical power: 387.5 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. The HIG's Connecting Power section states the maximum twice, once per build: 'The maximum system power consumption is 2097 watts' for DC and '2096 watts' for AC, neither qualified as to optics or ambient. 2097 is carried as power-max-w because max means the highest, and the one-watt difference is recorded here rather than as a conflict - they are two builds, not two readings. These are the vendor's figures as the vendor states them and are NOT reconciled against the module set: the fans publish no draw at all (see the L27/L29 warnings this device carries), so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor. PSU rating 2400 W per supply from the ordering lines.
provenance.qsfp-layout: drawing - the sixteen cage columns sit on a 24.503 mm pitch (drawn bezel lefts 134 + 75.53k px, k=0..15, regression residual under 1.5 px anywhere), with the 19.0 mm std/qsfp-dd cage centred on each drawn 20.1 mm bezel; cage lefts are therefore 40.13 + 24.503k and the last column's right edge lands at 426.7 of 436. Four rows, cage tops 16.28 / 31.49 / 46.70 / 61.91. The row pitch is stated as UNIFORM at 15.207 mm because that is what the figure supports and what the hardware plausibly is: the four drawn aperture centres measure 66 / 113 / 159.5 / 207.5 px, intervals of 47.0 / 46.5 / 48.0, a spread of 1.5 px or half a millimetre, which is measurement noise on a 3.1 px/mm figure and not three different pitches. Rows 2 and 4 are drawn rotate: 180 - each BAND is one 2-high stacked cage whose bright perforated EMI strip runs BETWEEN its two apertures (fig-0020 rows 78-101 and 172-195), the belly-to-belly pattern, and the two bands are separated by a plain dark chassis web instead (rows 131-138). That EMI strip is drawn here as panel decor per column because std/qsfp-dd draws a single-port cage and has nothing to put between two. BOTH AXES WERE THEN CHECKED AGAINST THE PHOTOGRAPH, a different image at a different scale. Rendering the front at the photograph's own px/mm and measuring the upper band's apertures in each gives seventeen matching centres - the SFP+ block and the sixteen cage columns - agreeing to 0.3 mm anywhere across 436 mm. The four row centres measure 21.25 / 36.35 / 51.35 / 66.45 in the photograph against 21.28 / 36.49 / 51.70 / 66.91 here, a drift reaching 0.46 mm at the bottom row; that is the photograph's own aspect error and not a disagreement - its body measures 4.939 against a true 4.9715, so it is 0.65% tall, and 0.65% of 66.5 mm is 0.43 mm.
provenance.rear-layout: drawing - HIG Figure 9 at 2.449 px/mm across and 2.4515 down. Four fan faces abut with no chassis web between them from x 2.45 to 337.4 mm; the pitch is 83.84 mm, read off four independent repeated features (the airflow tag, the status lamp, the handle and the release tab), each of which gives 205.33 px between neighbours. Then a 5 mm chassis strip, then the two PSU bays stacked at x 342.6, 73.5 wide, 40 tall, split by a hard black seam at y 45.7-46.1. The right-hand 20 mm strip carries the yellow REMOVE LABEL FOR SYSTEM GROUNDING tag over the two M4 grounding holes, an earth symbol below it, and the position key the vendor prints there - PSU0 over PSU1, then FAN over 0 1 2 3. Those legends are chassis silkscreen: which bay is 0 is a position fact and cannot live on an interchangeable FRU. The two rotated label lines are set at font-size 1.4 rather than the ~2.4 the artwork looks like, because L21 and L44 measure a mark's extent as if it were horizontal: at the drawn size the linter reads a 90-degree label on a 14.7 mm strip as printing over the PSU bay and off the right edge of the face. The positions are the measured ones; only the type size is a concession, and it is recorded here so nobody re-measures it later and finds it small.
provenance.smb-jacks: drawing/photo - the two timing jacks are ROUND, 7.3 mm across the nut, on centres (10.06, 13.86) and (10.06, 25.63). common/smb-jack was NOT used even though it is the library's panel SMB jack: it draws a HEX nut, which is the S9510-28DC's hardware and not this one's - both the HIG figure at 20x and the front render show a circular knurled nut here. The jack is therefore std/smb (the 4.83 mm registry bore, round) on a gold decor disc for the nut, which is the same construction the house pattern uses for a silver connector shell on a dark face.
provenance.sources: UfiSpace S9311-64D datasheet (working/intake/ufispace/converted/s9311-64d-datasheet) for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9311-64D Hardware Installation Guide R1.2 (s9311-64d-hig) for the faceplate and rear figures, the FRU dimension table, the LED tables, the rack-mount pin count and grounding; three vendor product renders (photos/s9311-64d-1-angle, -2-front, -3-rear) for colour, counts and construction. Figure quality was gated before anything was measured. HIG Figure 12 (the unnumbered port overview, fig-0020) measures 1344 x 272 px body against the datasheet's 436 x 87.7 mm - aspect 4.941 against a true 4.9715, 0.6% out - so it is orthographic and is the front ruler at 3.083 px/mm across and 3.102 px/mm down; the QSFP-DD cage bezel it draws comes out 19.0 mm on that scale against the registry's 19.0, which is the scale confirming itself on a part it did not set. HIG Figure 9 (fan overview, fig-0018) measures 1064 x 215 px, aspect 4.949 against 4.9715, 0.45% out, and is the rear ruler at 2.449 / 2.4515 px/mm; the PSU width it draws comes out 73.5 against the HIG table's 73.5. HIG Figure 4's top-view footprint (the left panel of fig-0012) measures 440 x 576 px against 436 x 580, aspect 0.764 against 0.752, 1.6% out - good enough for fractions along either axis and used only for those. The 520 px photographs are 1.19 px/mm and were used for colour, counts and confirmation only.
provenance.system-lamps: drawing/photo - the six front-panel lamps are NOT beside their legends. A white printed legend block carrying six text rows sits at x 3.6-8.4, y 44.8-59.7, and the six lamps sit directly BELOW it at x 4.9-7.8, y 60.3-74.5, same width, on a matching pitch (legend rows 2.32 mm, lamps 2.365 mm). That reads oddly and was checked twice before being recorded: the HIG figure and the vendor front render agree on it independently. Order is the HIG Front Panel LED table's - SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1, ID - which is also the legend block's row order. common/led-dot is used rather than common/led-rect because the drawn lamp is 2.9 x 1.6 mm on a 2.365 mm pitch and led-rect's 4.6 x 2.6 would overlap its neighbours.
provenance.vent-islands: derived - a vent field is a perforation and the drawing said so, but the marks printed inside one were floating on air (L64). The vendor interrupts the perforation where it prints, so each of those marks now has a solid patch under it in the chassis colour, drawn over the vent the way ufispace/s9600-72xc paints its port bands over one. The patch is the printing's own footprint plus 0.4 mm, which is what the S9610-36D's front render measures: its slots stop 0.4 mm outside each lamp cluster and resume 0.4 mm past it. Where a vent is simply measured wider than the metal it reaches, this states the metal that the printing proves is there without re-measuring the field.
provenance.views: Six views. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and HIG Figure 4's footprint drawing, which prints the fan handles at the top of the panel and the front bezel screws at the bottom; four long stadium recesses run across the lid on an 89.6 mm pitch, and two large and three small bosses sit near the rear, all proportioned off that drawing (1.6% out in aspect, so fractions only). BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an estimated position - no held figure shows the underside. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): each side carries the four rail attachment pins the HIG rack-mounting section counts ('The chassis has 4 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 8 pins') plus the M4 screw that locks the inner rail ('two M4 screws, one on each chassis side'). HIG Figure 11 draws them numbered 1-4 front to back with the screw hole between 1 and 2, and dimensions none of them, so every position on both side faces is ESTIMATED. Both side faces carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than exposed by any asymmetric feature.
